newsitem.title: USA: Lakes says secrecy on Bosnia arms a mistake - report.
newsitem.headline: Lakes says secrecy on Bosnia arms a mistake - report.

text.p: CIA director-designate Anthony Lake told lawmakers it was a mistake not to tell Congress about a decision not to object in 1994 when Croatia allowed Iranian arms to be shipped through its territory to Bosnia, the Washington Post reported on Sunday.

The newspaper quoted White House aides as saying Lake's statement had come in phone calls to lawmakers over the past 10 days, a move designed to make his confirmation hearings go Lake's appointment must be confirmed by the Senate, and his role in keeping the Bosnian arms decision secret while serving as President Bill Clinton's national security adviser is expected to be a central issue.

In April 1994, Lake approved a State Department proposal that the U.S. ambassador to Croatia, Peter Galbraith, tell the Croatian government he had "no instructions" in response to a question on whether the United States approved or disapproved the shipment of Iranian arms to Bosnia through Croatia.

At the time, there was a U.N. embargo against arms shipments to any countries in the former Yugoslavia. The Senate was also debating a controversial resolution calling on the administration to unilaterally end its adherence to the embargo and send U.S. arms to the Bosnian government in its battle against Bosnian Serbs.
A Senate panel praised the Clinton administration's decision to wink diplomatically, but said it should have told Congress.
In his phone calls, Lake assured senators "that in retrospect he thought it was a mistake not to have told Congress of the decision," one aide told the Post.
Lake also faces questions about possible conflicts of interest because he failed to take timely action on orders to sell off his personal holdings in energy stocks.
